evidence_basis: All364scheduler request histories and completed GPU prefill chunks
Per-request successful Mooncake DRAM GET log lines
findings: The high router means coincide with bursts of long returning prompts whose prefixes are loaded from Mooncake. All selected GET examples ran on the original replica.

The router takes its initial effective-prefill estimate from Dynamo overlap, decays one FIFO budget per replica, and clears a request on the first output token. It receives no early per-request external-cache-hit correction.

The green curve is reconstructed retrospectively from GPU chunks and excludes KV transfer time/bytes. Waiting requests can therefore contribute only a small suffix to it even before their external load finishes.
The60s trailing window retains earlier bursts; its peaks are later than many individual request arrivals. The400s downscale delay acts on replica decisions, not these gauge values.
limits: Per-request selection-time Dynamo overlaps were not recorded, so the exact purple contribution of an individual request cannot be recovered.
Before-first-prefill-step wait includes asynchronous cache reload and scheduling; it is not isolated network latency.
The middle illustrated request later encountered a proxy stream failure, after its measured first token.
The counterfactual field in evidence.json is an auxiliary simulation, not an observed router signal, and is not used for the measured spike table.
